Unfortunately this game is disappointing. Every run feels the same cause you just hoard every upgrade you get until there's nothing to choose from. Endless mode feels especially pointless because of this. On top of that upgrades themselves don't feel very meaningful either bacause most of them are just boring +2 stats/-1 stat. If this game was the first in the genre it would be awesome. But now we have so many VSlikes out there that this game just feels boring. After a couple of completed runs I frankly don't see why keep playing this game. That's unfortunate because the game looks very nice design-wise, but it just feels very repetative and shallow.

I'm surprised this isn't overwhelmingly negative. Maybe because it was just released so it needs some time to collect enough bad reviews. It's honestly so bad i wanna puke. Where do i start? The game is terribly easy. What's the point of unlocking stuff for your next runs when you can already finish game+dlc at your first try with the first and only available character (which is supposed to be weaker than the other ones) by playing absolutely casually without even paying attention to what skills you're choosing and being able to idle after about 5 minutes of gameplay melting everything on the screen with zero effort? Bosses were the only ones that required some running around. From the videos and screenshots the game might look pretty but it's honestly worse than a cheap mobile game with some random generic AI generated waifus just thrown there. Avoid this at all costs.

类幸存者的爽游 优点：1，角色成型很快 2，装备词条功能不繁琐不肝，内置的社区装备分享功能可以一步到最高级词条 3，伪随机的游戏设计玩起来很爽快 缺点：1，内容太少，除了一点NPC对话没有任何剧情，关卡和怪物种类少得可怜不说，BOSS也没做出很好的区分设计，在玩家数值起来之后同质化太严重，都是模型不一样的韭菜，10小时内就能从难度N1到最高难度N5。接下来除了重复割韭菜就没有任何新内容体验了。我28小时有10多小时都是开着电脑懒得关游戏挂出来的，还有几个小时单纯刷成就消磨时间，实质游玩时间可能就10小时，这10小时大部分都还是重复的内容。 希望制作组可以花些心思多做一些内容，多打磨自己的作品。

Really unfortunate case of another Reverse Bullet Hell half development, probably never to be actually made good, game. Now first up, the english in the game is rather reflective of my first sentence - it´s understandable what is meant but clrearly not looked over by a human being (I´m just a rad shiba) and as such really doesn´t get you into the mood for more. [b] But I should focus on the good stuff before anything else: [/b] - The demo was actually really cool, lots of locked stuff but straight up gives you the knowledge "vampire survivor this and brotato that" here´s difficulty modifiers and lots of stuff to upgrade. It lets you play basically a full run and get a good overview of what the game is about. - And you find out very quickly why it is called Artifact Seeker. The artifact system is clearly the best in the game, how you can reroll for them in a run, how you can put modifiers with a skillrange on them, how you can take some of them with you on a run, how many there are and how many more there are to come - Second up the loadout for a character, from meta progression skill ups, to a passive tree that sometimes even CHANGES how skills work or how they scale (albeit that is honestly the smallest part of it, mostly its just straight upgrades) and different strating weapons and upgrade levels with choices. There is just a lot to explore and look at, in the beginning almost too much but everything is pretty self explanatory soon enough. - Different map paths to sometimes play around with or well...actually not so much. But the events are actually well made, sometimes you get a reward even when failing, sometimes you have to fight despite succeeding at a check. Sometimes it has different outcomes, sometimes it is predictable and exploitable, that mix is great. And in events it actually makes sense just to have more of them, they are varied as is and just need quantity to have cool things happening in runs. yeah that was already most of the positive stuff I can really say about, the rolling for affix mods on artifacts is honestly the one system that actually is fun and creating unique runs. It´s a gimmick I want other such games to copy. [b] But there is just so much bland or negative stuff that will probably never change that really sucks the fun out of the game quickly, when it is supposed to be a grinding game [/b] - The number 1 thing that makes it frustrating is probably the culture barrier, there is just so many of these chinese bullet hell games that flood the market but never feel like they are more than an experiment at publishing rather than actually developing a good game. This game references Vampire Survivor and Brotato and is somewhat close to them. All the different routes: extra mechanics with skill trees and artifact vaults and special skills and even storybeats, could make for a really interesting blend of lots of cool things coming together to evolve the reverse bullet hell genre. Instead, at least for now, it feels like it will just throw some more content on top and call it a day hoping that quantity fixes the problems with the fun- and soulsucking faults of the base idea. Most likely it will be a neat idea basket with a cool gimmick that will remain forever at that level. - Now the biggest offense is obviously the artifact affix reroll system at the hub. It is way too cheap and makes runs basically a chore to get gems, or outright obsolete because you can just brute force roll what you want. It´s not "grind and find" a good item, it´s "have gems and just roll". It makes the biggest strength of the game so much less meaningful. - The difficulty modifiers are not something you can play around with. Some literally just take skill slots away...something the game can definitely do because in a 0 difficulty run you really can only use 1 or 2 skills and others don´t even reach the enemy fast enough before they plop...meanwhile on 50 difficulty where you would need all skills it´s basically impossible to get them up to that power or even have them available at all. Difficulty also scales not just uninterestingly by just simply making enemies tankier with invincibility shields or armor, but rather it also ups the difficulty where you really do not need it - in the beginning of a run before you have a build together. If the difficulty is too high for you its not even waiting for you to have a good run, because you won´t even get to that point. - The maps are wholly uninteresting. Yes it has that "stand in circle for x amount of time or enemies" but also not as RNG but literally at best only once per map. Also one buff you can´t choose. That´s it. There is some traps which is ok but they are rather unbalanced and not why you fail. - The characters are basically all the same. There is one dlc character which has an interesting mechanic with probability calculations but there is like 7 other characters and it is honestly pretty hard to say which one you play, they all use the skills in the same way (like said, the passive skill tree meta progression usually doesn´t change them) and they have no meaningful differences, at best its sometimes a special that is a little better than another but that´s a 1 min cooldown mostly anyways, so not really interesting. - Especially if you either struggle with a run or when you are at a point where you don´t struggle with a run anymore, it takes way too long to clear a map. It is either a whole 2 minutes of simply standing still with nothing to do because everything just pops before you know what it was. Or it is stuff littering the screen where you don´t even have space to move to anymore and wait to get overwhelmed. Either way there is nothing to do because that is the two possibilities that runs can go, no skipping allowed. At best you play 50 difficulty on the first map, that is literally the only balancing that somewhat makes for a fun gaming experience because here some range or speedmodifiers or attackpatterns on enemies actually make a difference and you actually engage with stuff like dodge mechanics to clear aoe traps from enemies...you know, the stuff that makes gameplay fun. You basically have that nowhere else in the game and most likely you will just fail here. Something is going wrong when failing (which is frustrating because like said you fail before you get a run going) is still more engaging than winning. So yeah, the game is bland with one actually good gimmick (artifact affixes/vaults) and some interesting systems (event-outcomes, skilltrees that change skills and character background stories affecting events). Unfortunately the gameplay itself is the worst thing a reverse bullet hell can be, a bore...or unbeatable. The rerolling of affixes is undermined by being doable easily outside of runs for gems, most modifiers are just generic +%, most characters play absolutely the same, most difficulty settings that would make the game more engaging are also making it so that it is hard to have synergies in the first place (and even the literal synergies). And I think there is no plan on making any of this any better. It will stay that way with another DLC coming out and more content thrown on top to no effect and that will be it. [b] Things that would actually need work but would also help: [/b] - "Death Must Die" would be a great mix, it has really interesting enemy mechanics and designs, cool map modifiers spawning to make every run feel unique and it has an itemsystem...the itemsystem is here obviously replaced by the artifact system but rather I think having items on top, that have synergy effects with the artifacts or the skills stats in a run or with their skilltrees would already do wonders for flexibility in runs. - Skills should work differently on the different characters and upgrading a skill should allow for another way to individualize what the skill does to complement your current run. - Better passiveskilltrees

练武功就练武功，变戏法就变戏法，总喜欢把它们混为一谈，活到今天也算个奇事 幸存者的快速局内成长的正反馈 爬塔的路线规划和deck build 局外成长又是有限天赋选择又是类RPG地图的保存装备 看起来元素很丰富，实际上每个都做的不是很好，元素之间的爽点有些又是冲突的，加在一起，更是不好

讲实话，其实看得出来制作组有在努力更新，在国产中也算是难得的了，但游戏本身也确实没达到一个很高的水准，所以我想提提建议，希望以后会更好。 1、地图背景急需优化。目前游戏的背景和技能到后期基本就是个光污染，别说小怪了，连boss都看不清了纯靠感觉找人找怪。 2、小怪和boss的建模有待优化。目前这个介于卡通与写实之间的这个风格挺怪的，精细度也不够高。 3、技能方面差异化不足。虽然看起来花里胡哨的，但基本都还是在打伤害，并没有见到什么本质上的区别，建议还是把各种异常状态和差异化搞搞。比如毒属性伤害就着重在伤害叠加上，与直接伤害区别开来；冰属性伤害就着重控制和弱化等。 想想还是算了，其实有些东西制作组不是不知道，纯是产能的问题，提了也白提就不说了。作品本身其实应该打个中评，但至少割草割的还算是爽的，就给个好评吧。

[b] 总结在前：最大的优点就是爽！真的爽，从第一局游戏就非常爽（甚至一度觉得，是不是有点太简单了？）。基本不会卡，如果有吸血鬼like的经验的话，可以很轻易通过前期难度，所以门槛相当的低。 第二个优点，就是制作组缝合功力不错，而且很勤快，始终在更新，好评！[/b] [h2]《神器行者：重生》 [/h2]是一款西方故事背景的roguelite游戏。局内是吸血鬼like，局外成长有酒馆等，不仅可以进去升级技能，还可以跟游戏内的npc和可用角色进行互动，提高亲密度。游戏内可用角色非常多，妹子的风格迥异，包括修女，魅魔等。。。。可以满足玩家的各种xp。角色虽然看起来是用了高科技画脸，但也能看出后期美术修改的痕迹，无功无过吧，如果不是铁血反人工智能人士，则不影响游玩。 游戏的音乐和画面方面，音乐也是无功无过的水平，没有什么记忆点，音效上后期如果技能等级拉高且复杂的情况下，听起来会有些聒噪。画面表现上，肯定是比传统纯2d的吸血鬼强多了，技能还是非常炫酷的，尤其在每个技能升级到max之后，那真是叫一个毁天灭地。 新玩家入坑的话，我建议先玩第一名角色，然后选整套的雷属性技能和武器，打起来非常爽，而且雷系比如闪电链等技能，非常的“小白”，只要瞄准个大概就可以进行攻击，闪电的连击效果可以攻击到大量的敌人。 关于技能升级，我个人建议前期先选3种左右，然后尽量把一个技能先升到满级，然后再选其他技能。 下面说说缺点：由于游戏的技能过于花哨华丽，所以再偏后期的时候会有些卡。然后就是游戏的系统，最开始的版本相对“简陋”，但是游戏体验非常好，后来更新了两个dlc后，系统逐渐变得臃肿复杂，使得偶尔会有些不知所措。但是这个话也分两说，因为冗杂也比那些不更新游戏的制作组强太多了。 总之，这是一款玩起来非常爽的类吸血鬼幸存者刷宝游戏，虽然也有不少缺点，但是瑕不掩瑜，整体是不错的，推荐游玩。 最后说说建议，强烈希望游戏加入联机模式！！！！！！！如果能跟朋友组队进行刷图，那真的是绝杀。后续也希望制作组再接再厉，更新更多的角色、地图、玩法等，然后可以推出类似赛季制，每个赛季有个刷宝目标，也能一定限度上提升游戏的寿命。是个好游戏，希望更多玩家可以玩到。也听说游戏之前下架的风波，但是重新上线了，非常厉害，祝游戏大卖，制作组好有钱更新更多内容。 更新新角色请继续上妹子！！！！！！不要来铁炉堡的矮人！！！！！！！！要大量妹子！！！！！ 联机模式快点端上来啊记得！非常需要跟朋友一起刷，如果加入联机模式的话，我愿称之为小菠萝。 制作组加油！！！！！

The graphics are what turned me off this game. There's no in-game antialiasing, and the mobs look very polygonal for a modern-styled game. Also, the rounds are shorter and spread out, which is not like other survival, bullet-hell games - probably a personal preference issue. However, this to me does make things feel more repetitive. There's also so much gear (artifact) choosing. I didn't mind this at first but it gets overwhelming quickly and all that effort/work on rng for what? It's not competitive; a single-player game. I wouldn't mind it if the graphics were better and the items seemed more unique and valuable to obtain/achieve. I do like the progression depth, but it's just missing something. It's a bit vapid.

The Artifact Seeker games layer a more complex progression system than usual over a satisfying diablo/action roguelike flavored vampire-survivors style horde killer. It has an odd mix of production quality; the game itself is rather polished, but the translations are not, and the "plot" sort of- isn't. It also leans more heavily towards grimdark "everything is evil" play; the stat boosting system is slightly opaque; you'll have to dig around in the town full of darkest dungeon like buildings to find the one that unlocks weapons. But there are so many systems that if you like that sort of complexity (you know that all upgrades are good in some way, so you can try to min-max a play style with a particular build) you'll likely enjoy it. Once you start to hit the content wall once things are maxed out, it loses some playability, as there aren't a huge number of events and you'll see the same ones frequently; but the core gameplay is fun, and there are lots of builds to try, so if you enjoy that kind of thing, you can spend the late game scumming for artifacts (remember to visit Katharine often and remove all the negative modifiers you can).

First things first, this game is really [u]cheap[/u] and that is doing some [b]heavy[/b] lifting, this game is like every add for those fake MMO games you've ever seen on mobile (you know those that are just renders with colorful loot and random high numbers) Graphics are AI generated at best and mobile stock models at worst but I have to give the game that it runs smoothly, even with a million effects and mobs on screen I did not stutter. If there's an actual human behind the pencil for the 2D images though then I'm sorry but you've mastered the skill of making AI looking art and you have my condolences for the worst art skill to have. Gameplay is janky but simple, you have HP, Cooldowns and you can move, basic attack, dash and use a special ability, in options you can enable auto aim, auto level, auto use special and more functions I didn't bother with, there are 3 modes to play, main, Greater rift (yes it's called that) and Endless, main was the most interesting one in my opinion, you're dropped on a map with branching paths with each area having en activity, Normal combat, Elite combat, Event, Camp and Boss fight, completing any activity (besides camp) opens up a caravan shop with reroll mechanics. [b]Combat[/b] is a box arena on a timer. [b]Elite[/b] version has more hard hitting high HP enemies spawn in. [b]Boss fights[/b] are also box arena style but last until you defeat the boss. [b]Camps[/b] are your combined utility activities with healing, selling, upgrading and 3 different shops with black market (for consumables), high end (mostly epic or legendary items) and skills (incase you don't like the ones you have) there is no limit to how many of them you do. [b]Events[/b] are just random little side story things that can mostly give you items for free so long as you have the required skill level, stats or sometimes trivia knowledge, most of them are generic but some of them are references that are sometimes very on the nose "[spoiler]defending some hobbits from a demon called Balrog[/spoiler]" but there's one mayor flaw with these events, they are [u]ALL[/u] 2D ink on parchment style, which isn't bad by itself, but the fact that there are in-game full color graphics of the events makes it horrible. [b]Endless[/b] mode is just long battles with no activity choice, I only played it once to get the achievement for clearing level 10 on endless [b]Greater rifting[/b] is like endless mode, but you can choose which items you want and in what order up to a max amount, with the catch being that you [u]Can't[/u] get any more/other items, the countdown is not for when it ends either but for when you fail, if you want to progress you have to defeat mobs as fast as possible and fill a percentage bar because failure means you can't go to the next difficulty, and when you go to the next difficulty then you start over from level 1 again with none of the items besides your starting load-out. (Also you get a lot more gemstones for progression in this mode) Progression is not anything new it's just a lot of basics mashed into one game, we have facility building/upgrading, character unlocking, character weapon & weapon skill unlocking, skill trees, stat increases, gems with more stat increases and an artifact collection where you can reroll affixes for items so you can start with an exact copy of an item with 3x+10%crit AND you can also randomly find it with those stats in a run, we also randomly have affection levels that just unlock stuff if you max them out. It's slop, but it's cheap slop 🤷

Normally I'd say this is what the game should be like, but only if I feel like I got there, you know, built stupidly over powered spells, but this was early game on my first play through. Artifact Seeker: Resurrection, developed and published by Lynkpin Game, is a fast-moving roguelite action experience that builds upon the familiar foundations of the survivor-style genre while introducing additional layers of structure and progression that give it a stronger sense of direction. Set in a dark fantasy world where powerful beings manipulate events for their own amusement, the game frames each run as part of a larger, almost ritualistic cycle of growth and survival. This premise is simple but effective, providing context for the player’s repeated attempts while reinforcing the idea that every run contributes to something bigger. The core gameplay follows a recognizable formula where the player must survive against increasingly dense waves of enemies in confined arenas. Movement and positioning are the primary forms of control, as attacks are largely automated once acquired. What makes the experience stand out is the addition of a map-based progression system that breaks runs into a series of interconnected encounters. Instead of a single continuous survival session, players choose their path across nodes that represent battles, events, or rewards. This structure introduces a strategic layer that allows players to plan their route, weigh risks, and tailor each run according to their preferred approach. Combat itself is fast and often chaotic, with large numbers of enemies filling the screen and forcing constant movement. The challenge lies not just in avoiding damage, but in managing space and timing abilities effectively. As players progress through a run, they gain access to a wide range of skills that can be upgraded or modified. These abilities form the foundation of each build, but the true depth of the system comes from the artifact mechanics. Artifacts provide passive bonuses and unique effects that can interact with one another in meaningful ways, allowing for a high degree of customization. Discovering powerful combinations becomes a central part of the experience, as certain synergies can dramatically change how a run unfolds. Progression extends beyond individual runs through a layered meta-system that rewards persistence. Players unlock new characters, abilities, and permanent upgrades that expand their options and improve their chances in future attempts. This sense of ongoing growth ensures that even unsuccessful runs feel worthwhile, as they contribute to long-term advancement. The steady accumulation of resources and unlocks creates a satisfying feedback loop that encourages repeated play, making the game particularly engaging for those who enjoy incremental progression. The inclusion of random events and branching decisions adds further variety to the experience. These moments can alter the course of a run in unexpected ways, offering rewards, penalties, or narrative flavor that enhances immersion. While the story itself remains somewhat abstract and secondary to the gameplay, these encounters help give the world a sense of unpredictability and depth. They also reinforce the idea that the player is navigating a system that is constantly shifting, shaped by forces beyond their control. Visually, the game adopts a stylized approach that prioritizes clarity during intense action sequences. Character designs and environments are relatively straightforward, but the abundance of visual effects keeps the screen active and engaging. Despite the potential for visual clutter, the game generally maintains readability, allowing players to track threats and respond effectively. The audio design complements the action with energetic sound effects and music that support the pace without becoming distracting. However, the game is not without its drawbacks. The complexity of its systems can be overwhelming at first, particularly when dealing with the large number of artifacts and their interactions. The interface does not always present this information clearly, which can make it difficult for new players to fully understand how different elements work together. Additionally, once players discover particularly strong combinations, the challenge can diminish, reducing the tension that defines earlier runs. Another consideration is its reliance on established genre conventions. While the map system and artifact synergies add depth, the fundamental gameplay loop remains similar to other titles in the same category. Players familiar with survivor-style games will quickly recognize the structure, and while the refinements are meaningful, they do not completely redefine the genre. Despite these issues, Artifact Seeker: Resurrection succeeds in delivering a polished and engaging experience that builds on a proven formula while adding its own strategic twists. Its combination of fast-paced combat, deep customization, and structured progression creates a gameplay loop that is both satisfying and highly replayable. For players who enjoy experimenting with builds and gradually mastering complex systems, it offers a rewarding journey that continues to evolve with each run. Rating: 8/10
